conventions.title: Signed and difference weight normalization
conventions.statement: Signed interference and model-minus-reference streams can have a nearly cancelling sum of weights. Scaling each stream to a total rate by its own sumw is invalid unless that rate and denominator describe that same stream. Preserve the generator-defined absolute integration normalization, exposure, sumw2 and covariance between correlated streams.
conventions.check: Trace the signed weight units and integration exposure; normalize raw sums with the declared common measure and retain correlated Monte Carlo uncertainty. Never replace signed weights by their magnitudes.

conventions.title: Landau-Yang constraint
conventions.statement: An on-shell colour-singlet spin-1 state cannot couple to two identical on-shell massless vector bosons, including the colour-singlet two-gluon state. Loop corrections do not evade these assumptions. Off-shell partons or additional radiation change the premises. This theorem alone does not forbid decay to massive vector bosons.
conventions.check: Check spin, colour, on-shell conditions and production multiplicity; justify any claimed evasion with an explicit amplitude and source.

conventions.title: CP-odd resonance and continuum
conventions.statement: A CP-odd resonance with CP-conserving pseudoscalar production and decay vertices need not have zero interference with the gluon-fusion continuum. CP-odd production times CP-odd decay is not a single CP-odd insertion. The actual helicity amplitudes and accepted observable determine the surviving term.
conventions.check: Compute the signal-continuum cross term for the supplied production and decay couplings and cuts; do not set it to zero solely from the resonance CP label.

conventions.title: Conditions for CP cancellation
conventions.statement: A CP-odd interference integrand cancels only under a CP-symmetric integration measure, initial-state ensemble, observable bin and acceptance. A CP-even observable alone is insufficient with asymmetric cuts. Distinguish mixing at one vertex from two CP-odd vertices in a complete amplitude.
conventions.check: Check the transformation of the full amplitude and phase-space measure including cuts, beam weights and binning before dropping a cross term.

conventions.title: Higher-order interference correction
conventions.statement: There is no universal interference K-factor. Signal, background and their cross term receive different perturbative corrections. Taking the geometric mean of signal and background K-factors is an approximation that needs process and kinematic justification, not an identity.
conventions.check: Use a cited or explicitly supplied correction within its domain; carry its uncertainty for the interference term and record missing information without inventing a factor.

conventions.title: Requested statistic and CLs default
conventions.statement: For exclusion without a prescribed statistic RAVEL uses 95% CLs. A prescribed statistic, confidence region or credible interval remains the primary requested quantity. conventions.check: Record the test statistic, tail conventions, nuisance treatment and requested confidence level; distinguish CLs from CLs+b and discovery significance.

conventions.title: Asimov and profile-likelihood assumptions

conventions.title: Goldstone equivalence and coupling conventions
conventions.statement: At energies large compared with the gauge-boson mass, longitudinal-vector amplitudes relate to Goldstone amplitudes with convention-dependent phases and perturbative factors, plus power corrections. conventions.title: Published likelihood and response information
conventions.statement: A reinterpretation needs the observable definition, selection and fiducial domain, rate conventions, correlations and statistical model used for the claimed quantity. A public histogram alone does not supply a likelihood or detector response.
conventions.check: Locate primary selections, efficiencies, likelihoods and covariance; retain missing inputs and scope limits explicitly.

conventions.title: Unfolding-model validity
conventions.statement: An unfolded measurement inherits response and regularization assumptions from its reference model. A new resonance or altered event composition can change migrations; agreement with the tabulated bins does not validate those response assumptions.
conventions.check: Find closure and stress tests for the published unfolding and compare the requested model with their tested domain.

conventions.title: Reference subtraction and covariance
conventions.statement: If a supplied full model includes a Standard Model component, adding it to the same Standard Model reference double counts that component. Form the model-minus-reference contribution using the same fiducial definitions and retain correlations from shared events and shared nuisance sources.
conventions.check: Identify exactly which reference was subtracted and match units, bins, cuts and perturbative order; account for shared uncertainty once.

conventions.title: Detector card and object efficiency domain
conventions.statement: Fast simulation implements the specific detector card and reconstruction model. Object efficiencies, isolation, overlap removal and working points are not universal, especially for displaced, soft or substructure-dependent objects.
conventions.check: Bind the card and working points to sources, census each selected object and validate the response in its kinematic domain.

conventions.title: UFO and model convention checks
conventions.statement: A UFO encodes model parameters, particles, vertices and coupling orders. Successful import does not establish physical consistency, a gauge choice, intended restrictions or the normalization of a supplied coupling.
conventions.check: Record model identity, restrictions, gauge and coupling-order selection and compare independent amplitudes or widths before using the model.
